title: Inductively-protected Andreev (IPA) spin qubit
authors: J. L. del Olmo N., F. J. Matute-Cañadas, A. Levy Yeyati, R. Seoane Souto, R. Aguado
abstract: The spin of a quasiparticle trapped in a quantum dot Josephson junction forms the basis of an Andreev spin qubit (ASQ): a semiconductor-superconductor device where the interplay between a localized spin degree of freedom and superconductivity leads to a spin-resolved Josephson potential. In this work, we show that shunting an ASQ with a linear inductor enhances its relaxation time by separating the spin-qubit states into distinct potential wells in phase space, nearly eliminating wavefunction overlap. The resulting inductively protected Andreev (IPA) spin qubit is equivalent to two fluxoniums in the heavy regime, one for each spin. Thus, the IPA qubit combines the long coherence times, low-frequency ground-state manifold, and large anharmonicity of a protected superconducting qubit with the operational advantages of a spin degree of freedom.
summary: The paper introduces the Inductively-protected Andreev (IPA) spin qubit as an advanced platform for realizing robust quantum bits. By incorporating an inductor shunt, it significantly enhances protection against environmental noise compared to standard designs. This theoretical work demonstrates how engineering the phase space potential can combine long coherence times with operational spin degrees of freedom.
main_problem: The primary goal is mitigating environmental noise (relaxation and dephasing) to build scalable quantum computers using superconducting spin qubits.
main_result: The Inductively-protected Andreev (IPA) qubit enhances coherence by separating spin-qubit states into distinct potential wells in phase space, achieving protection superior to standard ASQ or fluxonium models.
method: Theoretical analysis involving Hamiltonian construction, solving for energy spectra, and calculating wavefunction overlap ($\xi$) using both exact diagonalization and harmonic approximations.
model_or_system: The system is an Andreev spin qubit (ASQ) realized in a semiconductor-superconductor Josephson junction. Protection is achieved by shunting the ASQ with a linear inductor to form the IPA qubit, which behaves like two uncoupled fluxoniums.
key_observables: Coherence time ($T_1$), wavefunction overlap ($\xi$), and transition energies between spin states.
important_parameters: Inductive energy ratio ($EL/EC$), Josephson energy ratio ($	ilde{EJ}/EC$), and external flux detuning ($\delta\phi_{	ext{ext}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations, including the harmonic limit for calculating overlaps, which is noted to show quantitative discrepancies with exact solutions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate circuit diagrams comparing ASQ, IPA, and fluxonium potentials; they also plot qubit spectra, wavefunctions, and the overlap ($\xi$) as a function of inductive coupling strength.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the basic ASQ Hamiltonian to introducing the inductor-protected IPA model. It then analyzes the resulting potential landscape, derives spectral properties using harmonic approximations, and quantifies protection via wavefunction overlap calculations across different parameter regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses noise suppression in superconducting qubits by engineering the underlying quantum mechanical potential structure, a core topic for quantum information theorists working on solid-state hardware.
